reports.title: Ashleigh Timms: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: The NFCC undertakes, at the earliest opportunity, to seek to ensure that this Concern is reported into these committees to encourage debate and petition for such positive outcomes necessary, and as far as is achievable under this action by the NFCC, to, it is hoped, assuage your apprehension to this Concern.
promises.summary: Report concern to committees to address staff evacuation competence

promises.quote: Face to face fire safety training is now provided to staff. This training is provided annually by Pinnacle and is delivered at each premises. The training covers, amongst other things, evacuation routes and procedures, fire drills and fire safety measures. A copy of the training handbook provided to staff as part of that training is attached.
promises.summary: Annual fire warden training provided to all staff annually

concerns.quote: The operator of the premises failed to ensure that staff on duty were competent to carry out a fire evacuation
Fire Alarms in three units operated Sequence Care Group remain non-compliant with the 2013 British Standard Guidance
No clear and practical guidance exists on how specialist housing operators should manage the use of high-risk electrical devices such as portable electric fan heaters
No clear guidance exists regarding the fitting of digital key-pad locks on doors in specialist housing
Insufficient emphasis is placed upon recommendations contained within British Standards regarding automatic connections to ARCs in fire alarms fitted in specialist accommodation

reports.title: Paul Hutchinson: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: The Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 and the Fire Safety (Residential Evacuation Plans) Regulations 2025 do not appear to apply to the individual flats in ECSA because they are private dwellings
concerns.hazard: lack of specific requirement for PCFRA

concerns.quote: Staff training is not standardised for ECSA (or sheltered accommodation more generally) and may not include, for example, evacuation strategy, emergency evacuation plans, the use of telecare/fire alarm system and fire suppression systems

Fire Risk Assessments for premises providing ECSA and sheltered accommodation more generally may not contemplate vulnerable residents as forming 'any group of persons identified...as being especially at risk' (see article 9(7)(b) of the 2005 Regulations)
concerns.hazard: Fire Risk Assessments not considering vulnerable residents
